newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh spring sowing starts amid fuel shortages.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh spring sowing starts amid fuel shortages.

text.p: Spring sowing is under way in the south of Kazakhstan, but the hard-hit grains sector is short of fuel, a senior agriculture official said on Thursday.

"About 144,000 hectares have already been sown to grains in the south of the country," Zhanybek Karibzhanov, deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, told a government meeting on the economy. He gave no comparison with 1996 levels.
Sowing in the republic's icy north traditionally begins later.
Last month, the agriculture ministry said 19.4 million hectares would be sown to grains, with 12.2 million hectares of the total set aside for wheat.
The government is aiming for a 14 million-tonne grain harvest, clean weight, this year, above the poor 11.6 million-tonne clean weight harvest in 1996.
"We have many difficulties with material resources," Karibzhanov said.
Finding fuel is the main concern because the Kazakh oil sector is reluctant to hand over its production in exchange for grain futures contracts.
"We now have 300,000 tonnes of fuel, it is about 70 percent of our needs," said Karibzhanov.
